title: One link transforms a weak BCL-xL binder
subtitle: A five-state historical design series · one aligned receptor frame · reconstructed poses are labeled, not predictions

sources.label: Design of Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL inhibitors with subnanomolar binding affinities

compound4.label: Compound 4 · 138 µM
compound4.coordinateLabel: 3SPF ligand · aligned into the common 3SP7 display frame

cues.title: 1 · Start with one weak Site 1 binder
cues.body: Compound 4 binds BCL-xL at 138 µM. The teal ligand is experimental 3SPF; it is shown in the same aligned 3SP7 receptor frame used for every later state so the background never moves.
cues.detail: Experimental ligand coordinates · PDB 3SPF/B50 · common display frame disclosed

decisionCard.title: STATE 1 · STRUCTURAL START
decisionCard.note: The common receptor is a display convention, not a prospective prediction.

cues.title: 2 · Link a second recognition element
cues.body: Compound 6 makes the decisive topology change: a 10.6 Å connection joins the Site 1 scaffold to a complementary Site 2 element. Affinity improves by more than four orders of magnitude.
cues.detail: BCL-xL Ki <1 nM · cellular IC50 still >10 µM · pose reconstructed from the 3SP7 constraint

decisionCard.title: STATE 2 · FRAGMENT LINKING
decisionCard.note: This is the hard structural leap; the movie does not disguise its reconstructed coordinates as a prediction.

cues.title: 3 · Remove a linker carbonyl without losing affinity
cues.body: Compound 7 deletes the linker carbonyl and shortens the connection to 9.9 Å. Subnanomolar binding survives, while measurable cellular activity appears.
cues.detail: BCL-xL Ki <1 nM · cellular IC50 1.8–2.0 µM · reconstructed pose

decisionCard.title: STATE 3 · LINKER SIMPLIFICATION
decisionCard.note: The chemical endpoint changes; the camera and receptor do not.

cues.title: 4 · Delete a non-interacting side chain
cues.body: Compound 16 truncates the solvent-facing dihydroxybutyl group to methyl. The smaller molecule keeps subnanomolar affinity and improves cellular potency roughly threefold.
cues.detail: BCL-xL Ki <1 nM · cellular IC50 0.43–0.65 µM · reconstructed pose

decisionCard.title: STATE 4 · BURDEN REMOVAL
decisionCard.note: This is deletion for efficiency, not another pocket-filling growth step.

cues.title: 5 · Finish with a multiparameter redesign
cues.body: Compound 21 is not merely an ethyl addition: the shown endpoint also replaces the long carboxamide appendage with a carboxylic acid. The combined redesign reaches 61–90 nM cellular activity.
cues.detail: BCL-2/BCL-xL Ki <1 nM · cellular IC50 61–90 nM · reconstructed pose

decisionCard.title: STATE 5 · CELLULAR OPTIMIZATION
decisionCard.note: The literature series contains intermediate chemistry; this film compares the reported endpoints honestly.

cues.title: A real medicinal-chemistry success—shown with honest coordinates
cues.body: Link, simplify, truncate, and rebalance. The potency and cellular progression are experimental; the later 3D poses are clearly labeled reconstructions in one fixed structural frame.
cues.detail: 4 → 6 → 7 → 16 → 21 · one camera · one receptor · one ligand per state
